getting_started.label: Getting started
getting_started.title: Up and running in 5 steps
getting_started.intro: Follow this order for first-time setup, or load a starter template from the dashboard. One team is enough to get started. Time (punch clock) is optional; Clock Point remains the sign-in QR.

admin_portal.title: People through settings
admin_portal.intro: Chapters on the signed-in admin portal: People (Backoffice for colleague users, Teams for checklists and workers), locations, issues, tasks, calendar, reservations, dashboard, optional Time punch clock, optional ESG module, IoT Connect, settings and subscription (including data deletion).

internet_portal.title: QR codes on site
internet_portal.intro: Help for unit QR and Clock Point QR on site: sign-in, reports, unit check, reservations, tasks, photos, new-team-tasks banner and team leader features.

admin_portal.title: Statuses — administrative portal
admin_portal.intro: These statuses are used by administrators to monitor and control the full workflow.
admin_portal.new: The issue has been created; at least one task is waiting for the team to start.
admin_portal.in_progress: Work on the issue is in progress; at least one task is being executed.
admin_portal.done: All tasks for this issue have been completed by the team; the administrator can now approve and close.
admin_portal.closed: The administrator has confirmed completion; the issue is finally closed.

internet_portal.title: Statuses — internet portal
internet_portal.intro: These statuses are aimed at workers in the field and citizens (reporters) to show the direct status of a specific task.
internet_portal.new: The task has been created and is waiting for the team to start.
internet_portal.in_progress: The team is currently on site carrying out the work.
internet_portal.done: The work has been completed by the worker and reported as finished.
internet_portal.closed: The task has been reviewed by the administrator and finally closed.

step_1_text: Start simply: create one team (for example Hotel or Facility) and add everyone who carries out tasks. They sign in with name and icon. A team leader is not required. Link the team to your categories. Larger organisations add extra teams later, or import via CSV/Excel. Unit-check checklists are under People → Teams. Colleague users with login (administrator and employee) under People → Backoffice.
step_2_text: Group units into categories (for example: drills, plumbing, fitness equipment, office or electrical). Mark categories as Reservable if units should accept time-slot bookings, and turn on Allow reservations per unit (off by default). Optional: Require contact details (category and unit) for anonymous QR reporters. By linking teams to specific categories, WinProx ensures tasks are always picked up by the right team. Add locations and create units per location — via the form, bulk series or CSV/Excel import. Use Places → Units for a tenant-wide overview (location and category filters, unit count, status and unit-check pills). You can update unit names and descriptions manually per language. Optional: Allow unit checks (category and unit, off by default) for OK/Not OK rounds via the portal — separate from ESG. Link a checklist per unit (templates under People → Teams); the dropdown shows shared checklists and those of teams linked to the category.
step_3_text: First create one or more Clock Points (People → Teams, or Time → Clock Points if Time is on). Print the QR sticker or QR print sheet and place it at the entrance, warehouse or workshop — workers sign in here (name + icon). Clocking in/out requires Time (punch clock). Also print the unit QR from the location or unit detail page and attach it to machines, rooms or assets. Citizens and visitors scan the unit QR for issues, documents and optionally reservations. Workers first scan the Clock Point QR (name + icon), then the unit QR on site for GPS, photos and tasks. On the unit QR, workers can also run Unit check when category and unit both allow it.
step_3_text_time: Create at least one Clock Point (People → Teams, or Time → Clock Points if Time is on). Print the QR sticker and hang it somewhere visible. Workers scan the Clock Point QR to sign in (name + icon); clocking in requires Time (punch clock). Also print unit QRs. Then scan the unit QR on site for GPS, photos and tasks.
step_4_text: Issues come in via a QR scan, manual entry or (with IoT Connect) a sensor alarm. For each issue, a task is automatically created and directly linked to the responsible team. It is possible to create multiple tasks for one issue. Set a deadline and track progress via the dashboard, calendar and — for bookings — Reservations.
step_5_text: Workers carry out tasks on site via the unit QR portal (after signing in via Clock Point QR); when new team tasks arrive, a banner appears. Once all tasks for an issue have been handled, the administrator can definitively close the issue. Optional: ESG measurements, Time presence, IoT Connect and unit reservations — see the related chapters. Delete organisation data via Subscription (after export in Settings). For inspection rounds: the worker follows stops in a fixed order; on the unit QR they see progress and the next stop.
